newsitem.title: UK: Army says 20 soldiers hit in N.Ireland blast.
newsitem.headline: Army says 20 soldiers hit in N.Ireland blast.

text.p: The British army said on Monday that 20 of its soldiers were wounded by a double car bomb at its Northern Ireland headquarters in Lisburn, south of Belfast.
It said 11 civilian workers were also injured. It was the first authoritative breakdown of casualty figures.
It was believed to be the biggest attack involving British military personnel in Northern Ireland for several years.
The army said some of the casualties included medical staff tending victims of the first blast, which went off in a car park inside the base.
At least two of the victims were children whose parents are throught to have been army personnel at the Lisburn barracks, which houses a large part of Britain's 18,000-strong force in the province.
Five, possibly six, of the victims are in a critical condition, according to police.
No group has claimed responsibility for the attack but it has been blamed on Irish Republican guerrillas fighting British rule of the province.
British troops accused of enforcing neo-colonial rule from London have been the main target of Irish Republican Army (IRA) and IRA splinter group attacks in the past 27 years.
The attack was the first on a British target in the province since the IRA and its Protestant pro-British Loyalist rivals declared ceasefires in 1994.
The IRA resumed its war in February with attacks confined to the British mainland and a British army base in Germany.
